newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas slightly softer but market thin and quiet.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas slightly softer but market thin and quiet.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was marginally softer on Monday, traders and brokers said, although the volume of trade done was low and price movements were slight and limited to a small number of periods when trade was done.

The only quarters confirmed done were all from the second quarter of 1998 onwards. Some said that summer 1998 was traded at both 10.65 and 10.70 pence a therm, although others said this reflected the averages of individual quarters rather than a Q2/Q3 strip.
The price is consistent with averaging out individual deals done at 11.20 pence in Q2 98 and 10.20 pence in Q3 98, both of which were reported.

July was done at 9.90 pence a therm, at the bottom end of the assessed range on Friday, and Q1 99 was done at 16.85 pence a therm. Otherwise the only trade confirmed done was on the within day market or in the balance of the current month. The within day market was seen firm, with a steep backwardation in place from within day trade at 11 pence a therm to 10.40 pence for the balance of June.

There was some disagreement over whether the Transco tender, which will involve around 180 million therms of gas changing hands in storage and then coming on to the market later in the year, has yet been fully digested by the market.
One trader said it would have more of an impact on the market in the winter rather than this summer.

Others said it had already been factored into the market. And one pointed out that the absence of discussion or trade on the gas year from October indicated that most people had little view on which way prices were going to move, as the gas year is often seen as the best hedging tool in a volatile market.

On the IPE futures contract no trade was done at all, a depressingly common feature of the contract especially on Mondays. But settlement prices were generally lower, reflecting the slight losses seen on the OTC market.
Transco announced that Tuesday's gas demand is expected to reach 159 mcm, 37 percent of peak day demand, with the temperature forecast at 15.1 Celsius, against a seasonal normal 15.7 Celsius.
